title: Incremental Cognitive Diagnosis for Intelligent Education

problem.claim: Cognitive diagnosis must support online intelligent education data in which learners, test items, and interactions grow continuously.

gap.claim: Most contemporary cognitive diagnosis methods acquire learner and item trait parameters transductively, making them suitable only for stationary data.

contributions.claim: The Incremental Cognitive Diagnosis framework adapts cognitive diagnosis to online intelligent education scenarios.
The framework combines an inductive Deep Trait Network with an Incremental Update Algorithm, turning-point analysis, momentum updates, and a refined incremental-stage loss function.
The framework derives a minimum update condition using the monotonicity theory of cognitive diagnosis.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first attempt to investigate incremental cognitive diagnosis with theoretical results about the update condition and a tailored incremental learning strategy.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cognitive diagnosis is important for revealing learners' proficiency levels on knowledge concepts in intelligent education.
Existing transductive approaches assume stationary data, whereas online education data grows continuously.
The authors propose Incremental Cognitive Diagnosis with inductive trait acquisition and incremental updating mechanisms.
Turning-point analysis, momentum updates, and loss refinement target update frequency, update time, and trait stability.
The framework is presented as broadly applicable to contemporary cognitive diagnosis models, with reported extensive experimental effectiveness and robustness.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative experimental results.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical derivation or minimum update condition.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of effectiveness or robustness.
